newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices step lower again on technical factors.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices step lower again on technical factors.

text.p: World oil prices extended previous day losses in thin pre-weekend trading on Friday as technical chart-related factors outweighed supply-demand fundamentals, traders said.
The failure of crude oil futures to break post Gulf War highs this week despite several attempts led some to take profits ahead of the weekend.
"We just failed to follow through after several attempts to chart higher ground this week. The market is getting mixed signals now," a London broker said.
February futures for world benchmark Brent crude ended the day's trading session at $24.36 a barrel, down 21 cents from Thursday's close.
After several days of freezing temperatures, which earlier this week pushed crude near post Gulf War highs set in mid-October 1996, the forecast is for milder temperatures for this weekend.
"The wild card remains the weather," said Charles Gray, technical energy analyst at Prudential Bache Securities.

Resilient crude oil prices and weaker products prices have put pressure on refiners' profit margins as they pay up for feedstocks while getting relatively less for their refined product, traders said.
"The market is pretty neutral at these levels but poor refining margins in Europe are tending to keep a lid on things," said Scott Carter, senior oil trader at Tosco in London.
Low industry stocks in consuming countries were the main reason behind last year's price strength.
The lean stock situation, a result of oil company tactics to slim down stockpiles to cut costs and free up capital for other investments, has kept a floor under prices for weeks.
But there are signs companies are replenishing inventories. In the United States last week, stocks of heating oil, diesel and gasoline rose by several million barrels.
The entire energy complex came under selling pressure this week on signs that an armada of European gasoline cargoes were heading to the United States.
A senior tanker broker in London said at least 25 tankers have been hired in the last six working days to carry gasoline to the Unied States from Europe.
